label: Affine Varieties and the Nullstellensatz
notes: Open the chapter. Having played with curves, we now build the general framework. The deck follows printed pages 57 through 72 and introduces affine algebraic sets, their coordinate rings, the Zariski topology, and the Nullstellensatz, the theorem that makes the dictionary between geometry and algebra precise over an algebraically closed field.

label: Algebraic Sets
notes: Define an affine algebraic set as the common zero locus of a collection of polynomials in affine space. Every ideal of the polynomial ring determines such a set, and by the Hilbert basis theorem finitely many polynomials always suffice. These sets are the geometric objects whose algebraic shadows we will study throughout the rest of the course.

label: The Zariski Topology
notes: Equip affine space with the Zariski topology, whose closed sets are exactly the algebraic sets. This topology is coarse and far from Hausdorff, yet it is perfectly suited to polynomial geometry. Irreducible closed sets are the varieties proper, and irreducibility corresponds algebraically to the defining ideal being prime.

label: The Nullstellensatz
notes: State Hilbert's Nullstellensatz, the foundational theorem of the subject. Over an algebraically closed field the radical of an ideal equals the ideal of all polynomials vanishing on its zero set. This pins down an exact correspondence between radical ideals and algebraic sets, and between maximal ideals and points of affine space.

label: The Dictionary
notes: Read off the consequences. The Nullstellensatz gives an order-reversing bijection between algebraic sets and radical ideals, sending varieties to prime ideals and points to maximal ideals. The coordinate ring becomes the ring of regular functions, and geometric questions translate faithfully into commutative algebra, the strategy that organizes everything to follow.

label: Recap
notes: Close the chapter. Algebraic sets are zero loci of ideals, the Zariski topology makes them closed sets, irreducibility matches prime ideals, and the Nullstellensatz establishes the precise dictionary between radical ideals and algebraic sets over an algebraically closed field. With this foundation set, Chapter 04 studies functions and maps between varieties.
